chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated from Ibn Abi Sahban, who said:

When Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them) died, a chair was placed for Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) and he sat on it, while Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) was standing in a corner. When he had finished the funeral bath of Abu Ja'far, Abu al-Hasan turned to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) and said: 'O my son, God has made you worthy of gratitude, for a matter has occurred concerning you.'

key_terms.أبو الحسن: Abu al-Hasan (Imam Ali ibn Muhammad, al-Hadi)
key_terms.أبو محمد: Abu Muhammad (Imam al-Hasan ibn Ali, al-Askari)
key_terms.حدث فيك أمر: A matter has occurred concerning you (referring to succession/imamate)
key_terms.غسل: Funeral bath (ritual washing of the deceased)

ai.seo_question: What happened between Imam al-Hadi and Imam al-Askari after the death of their father?
ai.summary: This narrative from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the formal designation (nass) of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari by his elder brother, Imam al-Hadi, immediately following the funeral bath of their father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali. The contrast between the seated Imam al-Hadi and the standing Imam al-Askari symbolizes the transfer of authority and the imminent shift in the line of Imams, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of explicit designation within the progeny of Imam Musa al-Kadhim.
